subject: Re: MAP checkpoints and pricing iterations for Fintegrate evaluation
messages:
From: Samantha Parker <samantha.parker@fintegrate.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: Rajesh Gupta <r.gupta@fintegrate.com>
Date: Fri, 13 Feb 2026 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: MAP kick-off + questions on pricing cadence

Marissa / Redwood team,

Thanks again for the demo this morning. Rajesh and I reviewed the high-level MAP you shared and we like the proposed checkpoints (PoC completion, performance validation, org sign-off). Before we commit to the evaluation cadence we need clarity on a couple of items that will affect our procurement timeline:  

- Pricing bands tied to commit milestones: is there an explicit discount at month-3 commit vs. month-6?
- Ramp / guaranteed throughput: do you have a recommended commit curve for predictable SLAs?
- Evaluation credits vs. commercial credits: how will credits applied during the PoC offset initial invoice if we convert?

Can you send an updated pricing worksheet that maps discounts to MAP milestones and a sample mutual action plan with gating criteria we can circulate internally? We have an internal steering meeting next Tuesday and would like something concrete to present.

Also attach any template SOW or procurement checklist you normally use.

Best,
Samantha Parker
Head of Product Integrations
Fintegrate

[Attachment: MAP-Fintegrate-v1.1.pdf (PDF)]

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: Samantha Parker <samantha.parker@fintegrate.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, connor_obrien@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 13 Feb 2026 11:02:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: MAP kick-off + questions on pricing cadence

Samantha — thanks for the clear list. Attaching an updated MAP (v1.2) and an aligned pricing workbook that explicitly ties discounts to committed throughput and timeline. Quick notes inline below and I’ll follow up with Connor and Karthik for a brief walkthrough next Monday.

- Pricing bands: we typically offer a 10% conversion discount at a 3-month purchase commit (minimum monthly commit = 250k tokens) and an incremental 5% at 6-months if total committed usage >= 1.25M tokens. We can provide a capped accelerator for the first 90 days to smooth the ramp.
- Ramp: recommended commit curve is 25% month 1 / 50% month 2 / 100% month 3 relative to your target monthly throughput — this is what we use to size Dedicated capacity predictably.
- Evaluation credits: credit applied during PoC will be treated as a one-time credit against the first two invoices upon conversion; we do not backdate beyond invoice 1/2.

Attachments: MAP-Fintegrate-v1.2.pdf, RDW-pricing-revB.xlsx, Fintegrate-Rollout-Checklist.xlsx

Would love to set a 30-minute call Monday at 10am PT to walk through the spreadsheet and confirm gating criteria for the MAP. If that works, Connor will be on the call to cover performance validation criteria.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Sales Manager | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0142

[Attachment: MAP-Fintegrate-v1.2.pdf (PDF)]

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: connor_obrien@redwood.ai, markus_klein@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 16 Feb 2026 08:45:00 -08:00
Subject: Internal: suggested concession ladder for Fintegrate MAP

Team — putting a quick strawman together ahead of Monday’s call with Samantha. Key negotiation points and my recommended guardrails: 

1) Pricing discount schedule (non-binding until SOW):
   - 3-month commit: 10% off list for first 6 months if monthly commit >= 250k tokens
   - 6-month commit or 12-month amortized: additional 5% (stacked) if total >= 1.25M tokens
   - Early-exit protection: offer prorated credits for first 30 days if workload growth is lower than expected (limits financial exposure)

2) Ramp safety valve: allow one-time burst credits (up to 20% of monthly commit) in month 2 to accommodate initial spikes.

3) MAP gating criteria (what we validate on PoC):
   - Latency median <= 180ms for 95% of calls at target QPS
   - Token quality regression: pass baseline eval suite (PR < 5% false positives on our canonical prompts)

4) Approval path: any concession > 12% total discount needs VP approval (Markus). Anything that modifies SLA or financial terms beyond the workbook requires legal loop-in.

I propose we come in with the 10%/5% structure and keep the burst credits as a contingent ask during the call. If they push on shorter timeframes (30 days), we require markus sign-off.

Karthik

From: Samantha Parker <samantha.parker@fintegrate.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: Rajesh Gupta <r.gupta@fintegrate.com>
Date: Tue, 17 Feb 2026 14:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: MAP checkpoints and pricing iterations for Fintegrate evaluation

Marissa/Karthik — this is helpful. We like the 10%/5% ladder and the burst credits concept. Two follow-ups from our procurement team: 

- Can you make the 3-month commit threshold more flexible? We may start with a smaller pilot (150k tokens/month) and then ramp to 250k by month 3. We’d want the initial discount to apply on a prorated basis during the pilot and then retroactively adjust if the commit target is met by month 3.
- For the evaluation credits: procurement wants the credit to be applied across the first three invoices, not two. Is that feasible?

We’re happy to take the MAP and a short summary slide for our steering committee. If you can send a single-sheet summary of the commercial offer (bullets + figure showing the ladder), it would be ideal.

Best,
Samantha

Date: Fri, 20 Feb 2026 16:40:00 -08:00
Subject: Final commercial summary + requested one-sheet

Samantha — thanks for the feedback and for surface-level signals from procurement. Attached is a one-page commercial summary that implements two small concessions to accommodate your pilot profile: 

1) Pilot flexibility: we’ll allow a prorated 10% pilot discount for month 1 if you start at 150k tokens, with a retroactive true-up to the full 10% if monthly commit reaches >=250k by month 3. This protects both sides while keeping momentum.
2) Credits application: we can extend the evaluation credit to be applied to the first three invoices on conversion.

Other points:
- The MAP checkpoints remain: PoC (technical pass), Security review complete, Commercial sign-off. We’ve added explicit pass/fail criteria for the PoC performance tests and an owner for each gate in the MAP.
- Approval path: as discussed internally, any incremental discount beyond the 15% cumulative ladder requires VP sign-off and legal approval.

Next steps: please confirm the pilot start date and we’ll issue a draft SOW + DocuSign packet for signature. If procurement approves the one-sheet, I’ll route the SOW for internal VP approval so we can lock the committed pricing bands.

Best regards,
Marissa Cole
Senior Sales Manager | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0142
